title: Network Security as Layered Defense
description: A static SVG of six nested network trust zones from the untrusted internet to the crown jewels, with the control crossing each trust boundary and an arrow legend distinguishing ingress, egress, and lateral movement.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Identify the nested network trust zones from the untrusted internet to the crown-jewel data store.
Name the control that typically crosses each trust boundary and explain what segmentation defends against.
prerequisites: Basic networking: firewalls, the idea of a DMZ, and VLANs

instructionalStrategies: Hover each ring from outer to inner, naming the control at each boundary.
Trace the lateral-movement arrow and discuss why segmentation limits blast radius.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why is the DMZ kept separate from the internal network even though both are owned by the organization?
An attacker has a foothold on one internal host. What does VLAN micro-segmentation cost them?

chapter_title: "Network Security Foundations: Protocols, Firewalls, and Detection"
